_doc: PLAYBOOK 4.2: every promise (titles, thumbnails, hook questions, chapter loops) must be paid off; reviewer FAILs unpaid entries or gaps > 6 min without a partial payoff.

promises.promise: Title 1: the biggest living thing isn't a whale
promises.payoffLine: Pando ~6,000 t (> 30 whales), fungus 9.65 km², seagrass clone ≥ 180 km / ~200 km²; 'it depends on the ruler' list
9 of 10 sampled meadows = one clone; ≥ 180 km span ruler on satellite; ≈ 1 h 48 min drive

promises.promise: Title 3: a single plant twice the size of Paris, shown to scale
promises.payoffLine: ~200 km² meadows vs Paris 105.4 km², equal-area circles on the real satellite image
Same satellite view with the clone pins and the ruler

promises.promise: Thumbnail: tiny whale vs the clone
promises.payoffLine: Real top-view whale cut-out at 30 m on the satellite, pulled back to 260 km

promises.promise: Hook: how can one plant cover twice the size of Paris?
promises.payoffLine: Clone grows sideways by rhizomes 15-35 cm/yr for up to ~4,500 years; polyploid helped it cope

promises.promise: Hook: is it really one living thing?
promises.payoffLine: Genet = everything grown from one first seed, even in separate pieces

promises.promise: Hook: what else is bigger than a whale?
promises.payoffLine: Siphonophore 47 m, Hyperion 116 m, Sherman 1,486.6 m³, Pando, honey fungus

promises.promise: Hook: see them side by side on real satellite images, to scale
promises.payoffLine: Whale, pitch, Pando, fungus, clone on one EOxCloudless map

promises.promise: Loop: what counts as one living thing? (keep in mind)
promises.payoffLine: Ramet/genet; one first seed = one individual

promises.promise: Loop: can anything alive get much bigger?
promises.payoffLine: Trees beat the whale on height (×3.9) and volume (≈ 8×)

promises.promise: Loop: could one living thing be a whole forest?
Loop: what if most of a giant is underground?
Loop: the biggest one is hiding underwater
Loop: so is it the biggest living thing on Earth?
promises.payoffLine: Largest known area yes; Baltic Fucus spread longer (> 600 km) but area unmeasured; depends on the ruler
